newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel steady to weaker, low avails supportive.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel steady to weaker, low avails supportive.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil was unchanged to slightly softer on Wednesday with swaps falling a little, but low Russian avails were said to be still supportive of the cargo market.

High sulphur barges traded at $85.25 and then $85 fob ARA, which is within Tuesday's range but off that day's high of $86. Earlier, barges were talked $84/$85.50 fob for RMG material and $84.50/$86 for running refinery material.
"Barges are a little bit weaker but still stable, within yesterday's range," one trader said, adding that demand was weak. Other traders said there were enquries for about 10,000 tonnes.
Bunkers were valued steady at $86.50/$87 delivered on board for 380 cst while 180 cst was a little firmer at $92, traders said.
Low sulphur barges were quiet but buyers and sellers moved closer together with some sellers slashing 50 cents of their asking price to $96.50 fob and buyers upping their bids some $1 to about $96.
"We've had no deals in a while so buyers and sellers have to move closer together," one Rotterdam-based trader said.
